key_insight: A shallow Ritz neural network can efficiently solve 1D nonlinear diffusion-reaction and Allen-Cahn problems with O(n) optimization cost while preserving accuracy and stability.
engineering_relevance: This offers a fast FEM surrogate for stiff, singularly perturbed PDEs that captures boundary/interior layers on fixed meshes better than standard finite elements.
method: Use a shallow Ritz discretization for the nonlinear variational form.
Solve the resulting non-convex training problem with a reduced block Newton (rBN) method in O(n) per iteration for 1D.
Combine convex splitting in time with the shallow Ritz solver for an energy-stable Allen-Cahn time-stepping scheme.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments showing accurate layer resolution without oscillations, plus theoretical error estimates and unconditional energy stability.
watch_item: Performance and O(n) scalability are demonstrated for one-dimensional settings, so extension to higher-dimensional or more complex geometries may require additional algorithmic care.
paper_title: Efficient Shallow Ritz Method: 1D Semi-Linear Diffusion-Reaction and Allen-Cahn Equations
